\chapter{Synthesis --- Asking, and Answering}
\label{ch:spanish-synthesis-three-families}
\hlchaptermodality{28}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can hold a short exchange about what someone drinks and where they live, using all three verb families.}

Three families and two question words, and every word in the dialogue self-built.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Synthesis — asking, and answering}

\label{lesson:ES-C07-sintesis-preguntar}



\begin{quote}
Nothing new in this chapter. Say \textquotedblleft{}I eat\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}I live.\textquotedblright{} (\emph{Como. Vivo.})
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Something quietly enormous happened over the last four chapters, and it is worth saying out loud before you use it.

Spanish has \textbf{three} verb families. You now hold the singular of all three. That is not three facts — it is a machine: hand it any regular verb you meet for the rest of your life, and you can already say what you do with it, what a friend does, and what somebody else does.

Two question words turn that machine outward. \textbf{¿Qué?} asks \emph{what}. \textbf{¿Dónde?} asks \emph{where}. With them, the forms stop being an exercise and start being a conversation.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{The exchange}
\begin{quote}
— ¿\textbf{Qué} bebes? — \textbf{Bebo} café. ¿Y tú? — Yo también. ¿\textbf{Dónde} vives? — \textbf{Vivo en} Madrid.
\end{quote}

Four lines, and every single word in them is something you built yourself. No new vocabulary was needed to get here — only the endings, one slot at a time.

Notice what the questions cost: nothing. You did not learn a question \emph{form}. You put \textbf{¿qué?} or \textbf{¿dónde?} in front of a verb you already had.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the exchange above, both parts, without stopping
  \item it again, swapping in \emph{comes} for \emph{bebes}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:} Run it until the question and the answer arrive together.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many verb families do you hold? (\textbf{Three} — and that is all of them.) What did the question words cost you? (\textbf{Nothing} — they sit in front of forms you already had.) Ask where somebody lives. (\emph{¿Dónde vives?})
\end{tcolorbox}
